title: Queue Fabric Web Gateway is a narrow trust-boundary adapter
summary: The WebSocket edge exposes a fixed browser access point, not a general Queue Fabric client. Claim authority, principal, private bridge material and the ObjectQueueManager remain gateway-private; the browser sees only safe delivery/correlation material and semantic payloads.
invariants: The browser never receives Queue Fabric credentials or claim tokens.
The browser cannot choose arbitrary Queue Fabric queues.
Gateway delivery ACK occurs after semantic handler completion, not merely after WebSocket write.
Semantic handler failure yields NACK; connection disappearance releases/reclaims transport work without pretending the application rejected it.
Application/security authority remains in Wire UI/application code; the gateway never authorises business actions.
procedure: Bind one browser access point to server-derived IN/OUT queues and ACLs.
CLAIM on the private backend and expose only an opaque deliveryId plus browser-safe payload/provenance.
ACK after successful semantic dispatch; NACK on semantic failure; RELEASE on transport loss.
Validate outbound browser PUT against the fixed configured queue before using the private backend.

provenance.claim: Gateway-private versus browser-visible authority and fixed queue binding.
Opaque delivery acknowledgement and browser exclusion from Queue Fabric claim tokens.
